# WP7 script fixtures

This directory is the fixed WP7 handoff corpus.  It covers Bengali, Tamil,
Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Thai, Khmer and Myanmar.

## Cases

`cases.json` contains exactly 50 distinct sequences per script.  The same
sequences are shaped against two fonts:

- `fonts/<script>-real.ttf`: unmodified Noto Sans variable fonts from Google
  Fonts (`ofl/notosansbengali`, `ofl/notosanstamil`, `ofl/notosanstelugu`,
  `ofl/notosanskannada`, `ofl/notosansmalayalam`, `ofl/notosansthai`,
  `ofl/notosanskhmer`, `ofl/notosansmyanmar`), SIL Open Font License 1.1.
  The complete license is `licenses/noto-sans-test-fonts.txt`.
- `fonts/<script>-synthetic.ttf`: original rectangle fonts generated by
  `tools/generate_wp7_test_fonts.py`, MIT, copyright 2026 EXReader
  contributors.  They contain script-appropriate `rphf`/`pref`/`blwf`/
  `pstf`/`half`/`init`/`abvs`/`clig` lookups and mark attachment, so
  they exercise reordering and feature staging without vendor outlines.

`reference.h` is generated by `tools/generate_wp7_reference.py` with
uharfbuzz 0.56.3 / HarfBuzz 14.6.0.  It records glyph id, HarfBuzz cluster
start/end, advance and offset at 200 px for all 800 cases (8 scripts x 50 x 2
fonts).

## Cluster and metric policy

EXReader exposes syllable-level UTF-8 ranges for selection.  HarfBuzz exposes
the minimum source cluster start for each glyph.  The C oracle therefore checks
that every HarfBuzz cluster start lies inside the EXReader range, and that
EXReader ranges are monotonic and non-empty; it does not require identical
range ends.  Cluster values are not prescribed by OpenType: they are an engine
mapping from glyphs to source text.

Advances and offsets are compared with a fixed 1.5 px tolerance at 200 px.
FreeType returns integer hinted advances; HarfBuzz reports unhinted font units
scaled to 200 px.  The largest measured metric difference across the committed
corpus is 1.4 px (7 font units), while every glyph identifier matches.  The
tolerance is not used to hide glyph substitutions.

## Regeneration

```sh
python tools/wp7_sequences.py tests/fixtures/wp7/cases.json
python tools/generate_wp7_test_fonts.py
python tools/generate_wp7_reference.py
```

The C test `native-wp7` needs neither Python nor HarfBuzz.  Font hashes are
also recorded in the reference header and in
`docs/validation/wp7-windows.json`.
